rubrics.justification: The morphology description is detailed and broadly consistent with a 3AA day-5 blastocyst, including expanded blastocoel, good ICM, cohesive TE, and thinned zona. However, some image-specific details appear somewhat overinterpreted (e.g., exact ICM location/granularity, extracellular debris, no collapse artifact) beyond what can be confidently verified from a single image.

It thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, PCOS, BMI, prior failed cycles, sperm parameters, endometrium, and transfer timing with embryo quality and prognosis, highlighting how these factors modify expected outcomes.

The reasoning is structured and mostly logical, with a clear progression from embryo quality to patient modifiers to prognosis. Minor issues include somewhat additive/subjective probability adjustments and a few speculative links, but overall conclusions are supported.

Core recommendations such as SET for a good-quality blastocyst in a young patient are guideline-concordant, but several suggestions are not strongly guideline-supported for routine use after only two failed cycles (e.g., ERA, thrombophilia screening, NK testing, immunologic therapies, intralipids, routine PGT-A implication at age 32).

Provides clear practical next steps for transfer management and future planning, including SET, luteal support, metabolic optimization, and contingency planning. It is useful clinically, though some recommendations are more speculative than standard-of-care.
